items.postText:
📊 A claim denial isn’t just an administrative error. It’s an efficiency tax on a provider’s hard-earned revenue.
Too often, healthcare leadership treats denials as standard operational background noise. 
💡 Let’s stop calling claim denials "paperwork errors." It's a temporary freeze on cash flow, backed by severe administrative overhead.
But when you look at the raw data, the financial drain is staggering:
📉 The Cost to Rework: Industry benchmarks from the Medical Group Management Association (MGMA) show it costs an average of $25.20 to manually rework a single denied claim. For complex clinical or medical necessity appeals, that administrative cost can spike up to $57.23 or more.
📉 The Abandonment Rate: Shockingly, research from the Healthcare Financial Management Association (HFMA) reveals that up to 65% of denied claims are never resubmitted.

Think about what that actually means: Practices and health systems are paying their staff to process the exact same revenue a second time—or worse, completely writing off valid reimbursement for care that has already been delivered.

If your denial rate sits above 10%, treating this as a backend problem is a losing game. True revenue protection requires pulling backend trends forward to bulletproof the front-end intake and coding processes.

How is your organization shifting from a reactive "appeal queue" mindset to a proactive, front-end prevention strategy? Let's discuss in the comments. 👇
#RevenueCycleManagement #MedicalBilling #HealthcareFinance #RCM #HealthcareData #DenialManagement

items.postText:
DENIED AGAIN?
Don’t just resubmit. Understand why.

Repeated claim denials can impact your practice’s cash flow, delay reimbursements, and add extra pressure to your billing team.

Simply resubmitting a denied claim may not solve the problem. The key is finding the root cause behind the denial.

Ask the right questions:

✔️ Was there a coding or documentation issue?
✔️ Is patient or insurance information incomplete?
✔️ Did the payer request additional details?
✔️ Was the claim submitted correctly?

Every denial provides valuable insight. By identifying the reason behind denials, healthcare providers can reduce repeated errors, improve claim acceptance rates, and create a more efficient revenue cycle.

A successful billing process isn’t just about submitting more claims — it’s about submitting the right claims the first time.

A denied workers' compensation claim is not the end of the claim.

Denials arrive as a form. They read as final. They are not. A denial is the carrier's position, and positions get litigated in front of a Judge of Compensation Claims.

Common grounds: late reporting, a dispute over whether the injury arose in the course of employment, a pre-existing condition argument, or an idiopathic-cause argument. Each has an answer. None of them answer themselves.

General information about Florida workers' compensation, not advice about any particular claim.
